title: The sentence needs a real (finite) verb
subtitle: Form, Structure, and Sense · 22 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **22 of the official questions in Form, Structure, and Sense are this one** — 17 Easy, 2 Medium, 3 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The choices are one verb in finite and nonfinite forms, such as 'includes / including / to include / to be including'.
- When you look at the sentence, the subject has no main verb yet, or it has a compound predicate joined by 'and' where the second half is blank.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the subject of the independent clause and check whether it already has a tensed verb.
- 2) If it doesn't, or if the blank follows an 'and' that joins two actions by the same subject, eliminate every '-ing' and 'to ___' choice.
- 3) From what's left, pick the tense that matches the sentence or the verb it is parallel to.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The '-ing' and 'to' forms sound fluent and 'complete' when you read quickly, but they leave the sentence with no main verb, which makes it a fragment.
With compound predicates, the trap is choosing a nonfinite form instead of one that is parallel to the first verb.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The '-ing' and 'to' forms sound fluent and 'complete' when you read quickly, but they leave the sentence with no main verb, which makes it a fragment.
